title: SLO prioritization efficiency snapshot
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft of a short benchmark and narrative vignette that examines how SLO-weighted request prioritization (gold/silver/bronze) impacts end-to-end latency distributions and unit cost. The goal is to produce an internal one-pager we can hand to Solutions and Sales to justify a prioritized SLO product knob and to inform runtime admission policies.

What we measured (quick summary):
- Workload: mixed chat + embedding requests (chat 70%, embed 25%, short completion 5%).
- Priority classes: Gold (pinned warm slots, prefetch enabled), Silver (standard admission), Bronze (best-effort, lower batching priority).
- Target SLOs: Gold p90 < 120ms, Silver p95 < 250ms, Bronze p99 < 700ms (illustrative).
- Model: open-llama-32b-quant (representative medium-latency variant for tiered routing).
- Hardware: 8x A100 across a single region pool, multiplexed GPUs with slotization.
- Duration: 6h continuous, synthetic traffic shaped to reproduce diurnal mixes + injected microbursts (5–15 qps spikes every 10m).

Experiment configuration: (notes)
- Admission policy enforced before batching: gold requests preempt 20% of burst slots; silver uses remaining capacity with opportunistic tiling; bronze only accepts leftover multiplex capacity.
- KV-cache: enabled for chat, TTL 30m; prefetch on gold only.
- Batching: dynamic batching for silver/bronze, smallbatch for gold to keep latency bounded.

Key numeric results (aggregated):

ASCII table: latency percentiles and cost per 1k tokens by priority

Priority | p50   | p90   | p95   | p99   | avg tokens | avg cost ($/1k tokens)
---------|-------|-------|-------|-------|------------|---------------------
Gold     | 28ms  | 95ms  | 115ms | 180ms | 1,200      | 0.067               
Silver   | 46ms  | 210ms | 265ms | 420ms | 900        | 0.052               
Bronze   | 120ms | 610ms | 980ms | 1,900ms| 320       | 0.024               

Observations from the table:
- Gold meets the illustrative SLO p90 < 120ms in steady-state; microbursts push p99 toward 180ms but still reasonable.
- Silver p95 and p99 show heavy tailing during bursts; cost per token is slightly lower due to higher amortization (larger batch sizes).
- Bronze has significantly worse tail behavior but very low per-token cost; useful as a cheap fallback for non-latency-sensitive workloads.

Mini-sparkline (p95 over time across 6h, sampled every 15m):
Gold:  __/\_/\____/\__   (stable with short spikes)
Silver: _//\_/\_/\__/\_  (frequent medium spikes)
Bronze: /\___/\___/\____ (flat high tail during bursts)

Cost mix and effective dollars-per-satisfied-request (rough):
- Weighted unit cost if we preserve SLOs (allocate reserved capacity to Gold): 
  scenario A (strict): 55% infra cost to Gold, 30% to Silver, 15% to Bronze -> effective $/satisfied request = $0.0042 (sample)
  scenario B (even): 35% / 35% / 30% -> effective $/satisfied request = $0.0031
Interpretation: dedicating capacity to meet gold SLOs increases infra fraction for gold but reduces SLA violations. Sales-facing story: customers pay premium to avoid p99 shocks.

Qualitative notes and caveats (working):
- Synthetic workload: we did not replay a production tenant's long conversation sessions; results may understate p99 for chat-heavy, long-context sessions.
- Model choice tilts results toward mid-range latency; a smaller model (7B) or quantized 4-bit changes hop costs and reduces tail severity.
- Network jitter between client and region not modeled here; adding regional routing variance will widen tails for Bronze.
- Prefetch effectiveness depends on session stickiness; Gold benefits more when session affinity is high.

Actionable recommendations (draft):
1) Product: surface a simple SLO-priority slider in the console. Default: 70/25/5 (gold/silver/bronze) for enterprise tenants with burst SLA option.
2) Runtime: implement a soft admission cap for Bronze during sustained bursts (protect silver p95).
3) Observability: add priority-labeled percentile tracking and a "SLO coverage" metric (percent of requests meeting their class SLO) to the Console.
4) Sales collateral: produce a one-pager with a simplified chart (this doc's table + a short narrative) for customer pre-sales.

Next experiments (backlog):
- Replay 72h of anonymized production traffic for 4 tenant archetypes (consumer chat app, internal knowledge base, embeddings-heavy search, low-latency assistant) and compute SLO coverage under multiple split strategies.
- Test with model variants (7B, 13B, 70B) and quant profiles to quantify tradeoffs in dollars-per-satisfied-request.
- Add regional routing to see cross-region failover impact on Gold SLOs.

Open questions for review:
- What are realistic price deltas we want to expose for premium SLO? (sales input required)
- How aggressive should preemption be during a microburst vs sustained surge?
- Do we want Bronze degraded gracefully (throttled tokens) or outright reject when admission fails?

References / links (internal):
- experiment config: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-scripts/priority-slo (dev branch)
- related reading: CONFLUENCE-789 (slo pricing models), JIRA-OPS-221 (admission-control design)
